ontologyNodes.name: Umwelt
ontologyNodes.definition: Closed perceptual-active world of a subject, composed of Merkwelt + Wirkwelt; each organism inhabits its own Umwelt, which contains only subjective realities. Reframed in Part II as a voice in Nature's world-score, constituted by meaning-relations.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Funktionskreis (functional cycle)
ontologyNodes.definition: Closed loop linking subject and object via perception organ and effect organ; the basic unit of organism-environment interaction. Perception mark activates the cycle; effect mark extinguishes the perception mark, closing it. Reframed as Bedeutungskreis (meaning cycle) in Part II.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Merkwelt (perception world)
ontologyNodes.definition: Totality of what the subject perceives; the perceptual half of the Umwelt.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Wirkwelt (effect world)
ontologyNodes.definition: Totality of what the subject can affect through action; the active half of the Umwelt.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Merkmal (perception mark)
ontologyNodes.definition: Quality of an object as it appears in a subject's Umwelt; external mark "read off" the object by the subject's perception apparatus. Distinguished from the internal Merkzeichen.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Wirkmal (effect mark)
ontologyNodes.definition: Mark imprinted on the object by the subject's effector; cancels the perception mark, closing the functional cycle.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Merkzeichen (perception sign)
ontologyNodes.definition: Internal sign generated by perception cells; transposed outward it becomes a perception mark on the object. Recast as Merkton (perception tone) in Part II's musical framework.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Gegengefuge (counterstructure)
ontologyNodes.definition: Structural link within the object between perception-mark carrier and effect-mark carrier; the object-side nexus of the functional cycle. Replaced by Komplement (complement) in Part II's subject-side analysis.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bedeutung (meaning)
ontologyNodes.definition: Functional significance an object holds for an organism; evolves from relational property ("the only certain guide," U-F3) to universal ontological bond ("meaning ruled them all," U-M6).
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bedeutungstrager (carrier of meaning)
ontologyNodes.definition: Object transformed by entering a meaning-relation with a subject; bears meaning conferred by that subject. Replaces "object" as the fundamental category in Part II.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bauplan (construction plan)
ontologyNodes.definition: Structural plan governing the composition of either an organism's body or its environment; species-specific. Extended in Part II to environmental construction plans and subordinated to the Bedeutungsregel (meaning rule).
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Planmassigkeit (conformity to plan)
ontologyNodes.definition: Nature's structural design governing organism-environment fit; replaces teleological goal-attribution with non-intentional purposiveness. Oscillates between heuristic and metaphysical readings.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Kompositionslehre (composition theory)
ontologyNodes.definition: The general theory of how Nature composes organisms and their environments contrapuntally; the capstone framework of the Theory of Meaning.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Kontrapunkt (counterpoint)
ontologyNodes.definition: Point-for-point structural-functional correspondence between organism properties and environmental properties. "Were the flower not bee-like, the consonance could never work."
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Wohnhulle (dwelling-shell)
ontologyNodes.definition: The plant's equivalent of an animal's Umwelt; composed of meaning factors (wind, rain, sunlight) rather than carriers of meaning processed through functional cycles.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Subjekt (subject)
ontologyNodes.definition: Organism as perceiver and agent; constitutes its own Umwelt. "Without a living subject, there can be neither space nor time." In Part II, becomes both meaning-utilizer and meaning-recipient.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Ton / Tonung (tone)
ontologyNodes.definition: Functional coloring an object acquires in a given Umwelt (sitting tone, danger tone, feeding tone, etc.). Expands from perceptual affordance (Part I) to meaning-tone as compositional element in the world-score (Part II).
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Eigenton / Ich-Ton (self-tone)
ontologyNodes.definition: Intrinsic qualitative response of a living cell to any stimulus; fundamental unit of biosemiotic responsiveness. Builds upward: cell tone -> organ tone -> life tone -> organism symphony.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Urbild (primal image)
ontologyNodes.definition: Non-physical archetype guiding morphogenesis and cross-species meaning relations; the spider's web conforms to the Urbild of the fly, not any particular fly. Carries Goethean and Aristotelian (eidos) resonance.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bedeutungsregel (meaning rule)
ontologyNodes.definition: General directive that assigns a functional role independent of species-specific form; bridges carrier and utilizer of meaning. Distinguished from Bauplanregel (form development rule).
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bildungsmelodie (formative melody)
ontologyNodes.definition: Immaterial organizational principle directing morphogenesis from germ cell; plays on the "clavier" of genes. Declared inscrutable but real.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Stimmung (mood)
ontologyNodes.definition: Internal state of the subject that determines which effect image (and hence which meaning-tone) is activated for a given perception image. Structural parallel to Heidegger's Befindlichkeit.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Merkbild / Wahrnehmungsbild (perception image)
ontologyNodes.definition: Composite sensory representation of an object; higher-order than individual perception marks. Requires organized schemata (open/closed) in perception cells. Bees possess genuine Merkbilder; lower organisms do not.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Wirkbild (effect image)
ontologyNodes.definition: Representation of the act the subject performs upon an object; completes and alters the perception image, conferring meaning. Mood determines which effect image activates.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Suchbild / Suchton (search image / search tone)
ontologyNodes.definition: Internally generated perceptual template (search image) or functional orientation (search tone) guiding searching; can override actual perception images. A "free production of the subject."
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Moment / Merkzeit (moment / perception time)
ontologyNodes.definition: Species-specific smallest indivisible unit of experienced time (human = 1/18th sec); determines the temporal grain of the Umwelt.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Wirkraum / Tastraum / Sehraum
ontologyNodes.definition: Three interpenetrating subject-constituted spaces: effect space (directional steps), tactile space (places via local signs), visual space (visual elements bounded by farthest plane). No universal shared space.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Umgebung (surroundings)
ontologyNodes.definition: Objective surroundings; what remains when the Umwelt is stripped. The substrate all Umwelten excerpt. Nature-in-itself "carries and shelters all environments" but is never fully known.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bedeutungsverwertung (meaning utilization)
ontologyNodes.definition: Process by which organisms utilize carriers of meaning according to their structural plan; functional cycles reframed as meaning cycles.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bedeutungsduldung (sufferance of meaning)
ontologyNodes.definition: Passive reception of meaning against the interest of the receiving subject (fly in web, plant being grazed). Graded from harmless to ruinous; serves species-level equilibrium.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Naturpartitur (score of Nature)
ontologyNodes.definition: Comprehensive contrapuntal description of meaning-relations among all organisms in a habitat; biology's task is to "write the score of Nature."
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Bedeutungskeim (meaning-germ)
ontologyNodes.definition: Originary meaning-nucleus from which an organism crystallizes; the acorn is the meaning-germ of the oak. Final concept of the book.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Magische Umwelt (magical environment)
ontologyNodes.definition: Environment containing phenomena visible only to the subject, arising without external stimuli; includes search images, inborn paths, and innate behavioral sequences.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Reflexrepublik (reflex republic)
ontologyNodes.definition: Organism (sea urchin) composed of autonomous reflex persons coordinating without central direction. Contrasted with centrally directed organisms and the tick's integrated perception.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

ontologyNodes.name: Wirkzeichen (effect sign)
ontologyNodes.definition: Internal sign generated by effect cells; triggers motor impulses that produce effect marks. Counterpart to Merkzeichen.
ontologyNodes.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans

crossPipelineHooks.title: ψυχή (DA) → ζωή πρακτική (BCAP)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: DA's faculty hierarchy (nutritive → sensitive → appetitive → locomotive → intellectual) maps onto BCAP's ontological interest in the *praktikē tou logon echontos* (the practical exercise of the being that has logos).
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This hook grounds the argument that Aristotle's psychology is already proto-existential in its teleological structure.

crossPipelineHooks.title: φαντασία (DA) → Erschlossenheit / Being-in-the-World (B&T)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: DA III.8's thesis that "the soul is in a way all existing things" (432a1--3) is a locus Heidegger repeatedly engages.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This hook is load-bearing for the dissertation's central argument.

crossPipelineHooks.title: αἴσθησις (DA) → Befindlichkeit (B&T)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The critical parallel lies in the *receptive* character of both *aisthēsis* and *Befindlichkeit*.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This hook supports the argument that *aisthēsis* is proto-attunement: an embodied, world-directed, receptive mode of being that discloses the environment's character through the organism's own structural calibration.

crossPipelineHooks.title: φάντασμα (DA) → Merkbild (Uexkull)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The structural parallel is precise: both *phantasma* and *Merkbild* are organism-internal perceptual residues that guide action in the absence of current stimulation.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This hook supports the argument that phantasia is the Aristotelian ancestor of the biosemiotic *Merkbild* -- but with a crucial ontological difference.

crossPipelineHooks.title: ὄρεξις + φαντασία → κίνησις (DA) → Ambient Rhetoric (Rickert)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The DA III.9--11 circuit (phantasia → orexis → kinēsis) is the Aristotelian mechanism by which appearances produce bodily movement through the mediation of desire.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This hook establishes that the phantasia-orexis-kinēsis circuit of DA III is the Aristotelian foundation for Rickert's ambient rhetoric.

crossPipelineHooks.title: αἴσθησις as Form-Reception (DA) → Weltarmut / Weltbildend (GA 29/30 via Uexkull)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: DA's distinction between plant (affected by forms with matter = no perception) and animal (receives forms without matter = genuine perception) is a precursor to Heidegger's stone/animal distinction.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This hook positions the wax-signet principle as the Aristotelian version of the *Weltbildung* threshold.

crossPipelineHooks.title: κίνησις in MA → BCAP on κίνησις [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: κίνησις (C3) — animal locomotion as a specific instantiation of the general concept of movement; requires both an internal immovable point and an external immovable ground; caused proximately by desire.

crossPipelineHooks.title: φαντασία as practical mover → BCAP on φαντασία [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: φαντασία (C2) — presents objects to desire as a "faculty of discrimination" (700b19-21); can produce involuntary movements "without express mandate of the intellect" (703b6-8); mediates between perception and action.

crossPipelineHooks.title: ὄρεξις and the practical syllogism → BCAP on ὄρεξις and πρᾶξις [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: ὄρεξις (C1) as the proximate efficient cause of action; the practical syllogism (C4) as the logical structure of desire-driven action.

crossPipelineHooks.title: σύμφυτον πνεῦμα → Embodied action [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: σύμφυτον πνεῦμα (I2) — the connate spirit as the bodily medium transmitting desire's motive force to the limbs through expansion and contraction.

crossPipelineHooks.title: The puppet analogy → Automaticity and ambient action [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: The puppet (αὐτόματον) analogy — "the movements of animals may be compared with those of automatic puppets" (701b2); a tiny occasion sets off cascading movement.

crossPipelineHooks.sourceConcept: τὸ ἀγαθόν as final cause of movement
crossPipelineHooks.title: τὸ ἀγαθόν as final cause of movement → Teleological structure of action [INTERP-low]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: τὸ ἀγαθόν (C5) — the good (actual or apparent) as the final cause initiating desire and thus movement; "not every intelligible object, but only the end in the domain of conduct" (700b25).

crossPipelineHooks.title: χρῶμα → Sense and Sensibilia colour theory [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: χρῶμα (C1) — simple colours derived from the four elements; intermediate colours from mixture and blending.

crossPipelineHooks.title: πέψις (maturation) → Biological teleology [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: πέψις (C4) — the maturation process driving chromatic change in plants and animals through heat, nutriment, and moisture.

crossPipelineHooks.title: λευκόν as deviation/weakness → Privation ontology [INTERP-low]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: White as the colour of "deviation from natural colour" (798a25-b5), associated with weakness, ageing, and premature maturation.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Dyeing analogy → Techne and nature [INTERP-low]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: βαφή (I3) — dyeing as the paradigm case of colour transference; used as analogy for natural processes (fruit maturation, animal colouring).

crossPipelineHooks.title: φάντασμα as memory-image → B&T temporality [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: φάντασμα (C3) — the dual-aspect memory-image that functions simultaneously as an object of contemplation in itself and as a likeness (εἰκών) of the thing remembered.

crossPipelineHooks.title: μνήμη / ἀνάμνησις → B&T retention and retrieval [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: μνήμη (C1) as passive retention conditioned by time; ἀνάμνησις (C2) as active inferential recovery through sequential reactivation of movements.

crossPipelineHooks.title: ἀνάμνησις as ζήτησις → Rhetorical τόποι [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: ἀνάμνησις operates through "places" (τόποι) — starting-points from which recollection proceeds by hunting up associations (similarity, contrariety, contiguity).

crossPipelineHooks.title: κίνησις (residual movements) → BCAP on κίνησις [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: κίνησις (C5) — residual physiological movements left by perception; their sequential reactivation constitutes recollection; movements succeed one another by nature, custom, or association.

crossPipelineHooks.title: τὸ πρῶτον αἰσθητικόν (common sense) → Sense and Sensibilia [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: τὸ πρῶτον αἰσθητικόν (I1) — the primary perceptive faculty / common sense, which cognizes time, magnitude, and motion; the organ to which memory essentially belongs.

crossPipelineHooks.title: τύπος (wax-seal model) → Embodied cognition [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: τύπος (I3) — the impression stamped in the soul and its bodily seat; the wax-seal analogy (450a27-b1); physiological conditions (moisture, hardness) explain individual differences.

crossPipelineHooks.title: ψόφος / πληγή → De Anima II.8 sound theory [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: ψόφος (C1) — all sounds arise from the impact (πληγή) of air against bodies; the De Audibilibus provides the detailed material acoustics.

crossPipelineHooks.title: σαφές (clearness) across modalities → Common sensibles and cross-modal analogy [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: σαφές (C4) — clearness in sound analogous to clearness in colour; the claim that the strongest, purest stimuli produce the most distinct impressions across both modalities.

crossPipelineHooks.title: τραχύς (roughness) → Touch and cross-modal perception [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: τραχύς (I2) — rough sounds arise when the impact is divided and dispersed, "each portion striking separately"; compared to rough objects touching the skin.

crossPipelineHooks.title: πνεῦμα (breath) → MA σύμφυτον πνεῦμα [INTERP-low]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: πνεῦμα (C3) — breath as the material cause of vocal sound; its force, quantity, and manner of expulsion determine vocal quality.

crossPipelineHooks.title: συμφωνία (concord) → Ratio-theory in De Sensu [INTERP-low]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: συμφωνία (I3) — musical concords arise from overlapping note-impacts causing intermediate sounds to escape notice.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Connection
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The BCAP analysis covers Aristotle's *Rhetoric* lectures (GA 18, Grundbegriffe der aristotelischen Philosophie), where sections 25--28 treat κίνησις as a fundamental concept (Grundbegriff) in relation to δύναμις and ἐνέργεια.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Specific hooks
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: - **Physics IV.11 (219b1--2)**: "Time is the number of motion in respect of before and after." B&T SS78 directly engages this definition, arguing it captures only "world-time" (Weltzeit) — time as public, measurable, and derived from Dasein's primordial temporality.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Connection
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Physics II.1 establishes the foundational distinction between nature (φύσις) and art (τέχνη): nature has its principle of motion and rest in the thing itself; art has its principle in the maker (192b20--33).

crossPipelineHooks.title: Specific hooks
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: - **Physics II.1 (192b20--23)**: Nature as internal principle.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Integration points
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: [INTERP-high] — Uexkull's Naturtechnik challenges the Aristotelian phusis/technē distinction by arguing that organisms exhibit a technical character that is *natural* — not imposed from without but generated from within according to a plan.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Connection

crossPipelineHooks.title: Connection
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Physics VII.2 argues that the mover and the moved must always be in contact, and demonstrates this for alteration by induction from sense-perception: "air is continuous with colour, colour with sight" (244b2--245a5).

crossPipelineHooks.title: Connection
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Physics IV.14's claim that time depends on soul as counter (223a21--26) connects directly to On Memory's account of temporal perception: memory is always of the past and involves a lapse of time (449b25).

crossPipelineHooks.title: Connection
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The unmoved mover argument of Physics VIII is restated and deepened in Metaphysics XII.6--7 (1071b--1072b), where the unmoved mover is identified with pure thought thinking itself (noēsis noēseōs) and is said to move as an object of desire (kinei hōs erōmenon, 1072b3).

crossPipelineHooks.title: αἴσθησις → Uexküll Merkwelt [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: αἴσθησις (C3) — sensation as a joint function of soul and body, mediated by external elements; the senses are not deceived about their proper objects (τὰ ἴδια αἰσθητά).

crossPipelineHooks.title: τὸ διαφανές as μεταξύ → B&T world-disclosure [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: τὸ διαφανές (C1) — the transparent as medium (μεταξύ) between perceiver and perceived; a "common nature and power" not peculiar to any element.

crossPipelineHooks.title: κοινὴ αἴσθησις → BCAP on φαντασία [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: κοινὴ αἴσθησις (C4) — the common sense faculty, numerically one but specifically different for each sense-province; perceives time, magnitude, and motion; the faculty through which simultaneous cross-modal perception occurs.

crossPipelineHooks.title: δύναμις/ἐνέργεια in perception → BCAP on δύναμις [INTERP-high]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: δύναμις/ἐνέργεια (C6) — potentiality/actuality applied to perceptibility; sensible qualities exist potentially below the threshold of perception and become actual only at sufficient scale.

crossPipelineHooks.title: χρῶμα / μῖξις → On Colours colour theory [INTERP-low]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: χρῶμα (C2) as the limit of the transparent; μῖξις (C5) as genuine blending vs. juxtaposition.

crossPipelineHooks.title: χυμός / ὀσμή → Sense-media and environmental perception [INTERP-med]
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: **Aristotelian concept**: χυμός (I2) as savour generated by the sapid dry in the moist; ὀσμή (I3) as odour operating through air and water.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Imagination
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Phantasia is the faculty in virtue of which the animal sees his object as an object of a certain sort, giving perception potentially motivating content.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The use of phantasia in action-contexts and its broad connection with phainetai throughout Aristotle suggest this interpretation.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Image
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The expository passages on decaying sense use aisthēmata rather than phantasmata or phantasia, suggesting phantasia is not necessarily pictorial.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Although Mem. 451a15-16 uses phantasma for memory-image, the detailed theoretical passages discuss perceptual after-images with reference to aisthēmata, not phantasmata.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Movement/Change
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Motion always requires both phantasia and desire together.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: DA 432b15 states motion occurs with both phantasia and orexis; 433b26-30 says animals cannot desire without phantasia.

crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Motion always requires both phantasia and desire together.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: DA 432b15 states motion occurs with both phantasia and orexis; 433b26-30 says animals cannot desire without phantasia.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on State/Disposition
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle invokes images to explain memory and dreaming specifically in connection with his physiological theory of decaying sense, not as part of general psychological doctrine.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Memory and dreaming are explained via images that are likenesses of things in the world, but this is tied to the theory of persisting kinēseis rather than broader psychological commitments.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Desire
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Motion always requires both phantasia and desire together.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: DA 432b15 states motion occurs with both phantasia and orexis; 433b26-30 says animals cannot desire without phantasia.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Perception
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Despite initial suggestions of disjunctive operation, Aristotle later assigns phantasia a broader role as involved in every action.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: At MA 701a18ff, phantasia prepares desire whether or not actual perceiving occurs, coming about through thought or sense-perception.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Destruktion
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Any one of the three kritika can operate without the other two, combined with orexis, to produce action.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The sketchy account in MA 6 suggests desire + sense-perception or desire + thinking would suffice to move the animal without phantasia involvement.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Embodiment / Embodied Cognition
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Objections to image theory based on the ontological status of images (what sort of entity, in what space) are not compelling.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Accounting for images within a physicalist picture of mind is no more difficult in principle than accounting for sensations, and the location problem for images is analogous to the familiar problem about where sensations are located.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Cause
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: DA III.3 cannot be coherently interpreted as building up to the decaying-sense discussion as definitive summary.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Earlier in III.3, phantasia is invoked to explain error in presence of object (sun-example), contrasted with doxa, said to be 'in our power' as active conjuring, and used to explain unclear perception of actual objects—none of which fit narrow decaying-sense theory.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on φάντασμα
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The expository passages on decaying sense use aisthēmata rather than phantasmata or phantasia, suggesting phantasia is not necessarily pictorial.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Although Mem. 451a15-16 uses phantasma for memory-image, the detailed theoretical passages discuss perceptual after-images with reference to aisthēmata, not phantasmata.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Contradiction (PNC)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle's denial that thinking is physical commits him to a messy over-complexity requiring an extra phantasia in practical cases.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The thought of the sun's true size must be accompanied by symbolizing that is likely the same as the pre-judgmental phantasia seeing it as a foot wide, yet action theory forces insertion of an extra phantasia.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Presence-at-hand
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: DA III.3's contrast of phantasia with aisthesis must be used cautiously to explain action passages because Aristotle seems to be thinking primarily of phantasia in the absence of the perceptible object.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The statement that aisthesis but not phantasia is always going on (428b8-9) might indicate we have phantasia only when the object is not present.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on εἰκών
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle's memory theory may use resemblance as criterion of symbolization but still doesn't fully amount to a pictorial image-theory.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: At 450a25ff the 'image' in isolation is either a theōrēma or phantasma (theōrēma unlikely to be pictorial), and at 451a1 a noēma contrasted with mnēmoneuma suggests memory can work through non-pictorial thoughts regarded as referring to the past.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Wirkbild (effect image)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: To be moved to action an animal has to become aware of something qua what-it-is-called (e.g., man as man), not just qua its perceptible quality (e.g., as pale).
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: When we perceive a rose by sight, it is the rose qua white that acts upon sight, not the rose qua rose; but action requires awareness of unified objects under descriptions.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Merkbild / Wahrnehmungsbild (perception image)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Imagining need not involve anything like a picture.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Image theory persistently ignores auditory, olfactory, and tactile images and has no account showing they function like visual picture-images.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Suchbild / Suchton (search image / search tone)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: When we actively focus on some object in our environment, separating it from its context and seeing it as a certain thing, the faculty of phantasia or the phantasia-aspect of aisthesis is called into play.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: We are always passively receiving perceptual stimuli, but active focusing requires something more than mere passive reception.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on πρὸ ὀμμάτων ποιεῖν
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The phrase kata metaphoran at DA 428a1-4 does not rule out general uses of phantasia connected with phainetai in favor of image-cases.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle uses kata metaphoran consistently to designate conscious shifts away from basic ordinary usage (examples: oxu for pitch, dunamis in mathematics, andreios for quasi-courageous), not to contrast technical with ordinary senses.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on The Continuous
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The two claims of image theory are logically independent.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: One might hold that images must be similar without granting there is more to be found in them than was intentionally put there, or insist on picture-like density while allowing conventional representation.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Authenticity/Inauthenticity
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: In many cases of imagining, there is never more content than what the imaginer intentionally put in.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Sartre, Ishiguro, and possibly Wittgenstein claim imagining is like sketching without stepping back to see what one has made; an image has just the content with which we invest it.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Reality
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle's denial that thinking is physical commits him to a messy over-complexity requiring an extra phantasia in practical cases.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The thought of the sun's true size must be accompanied by symbolizing that is likely the same as the pre-judgmental phantasia seeing it as a foot wide, yet action theory forces insertion of an extra phantasia.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Being qua Being
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: In explanation of action, the philosopher must begin with how the world looks to the particular creature, not with unprocessed sensory material.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Just as in science generally the philosopher must begin with and return to the phainomena (not 'pure' or 'raw' data), so in action explanation he must begin with the way the world looks to the creature.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Signs
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Similarity is neither necessary nor sufficient for pictorial representation.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: An object closely resembles but does not represent a copy of itself; conversely, reference can be secured independently of resemblance, as when a fish symbolizes Christ or a bird symbolizes the Holy Spirit.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Metaphor
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The phrase kata metaphoran at DA 428a1-4 does not rule out general uses of phantasia connected with phainetai in favor of image-cases.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle uses kata metaphoran consistently to designate conscious shifts away from basic ordinary usage (examples: oxu for pitch, dunamis in mathematics, andreios for quasi-courageous), not to contrast technical with ordinary senses.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on μεταφορά
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The phrase kata metaphoran at DA 428a1-4 does not rule out general uses of phantasia connected with phainetai in favor of image-cases.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle uses kata metaphoran consistently to designate conscious shifts away from basic ordinary usage (examples: oxu for pitch, dunamis in mathematics, andreios for quasi-courageous), not to contrast technical with ordinary senses.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Curiosity
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: To move a creature to action, an object must appear to him through selection, marking off, organization, and interpretation.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This is, desire aside, what it is to see the object.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Circumspection
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: To move a creature to action, an object must appear to him through selection, marking off, organization, and interpretation.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This is, desire aside, what it is to see the object.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Interpretation
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The basic insight underlying Aristotle's phantasia theory is that perceptual reception is inseparable from interpretation.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: We cannot explain an animal's perception of something as a distinct feature in his environment with reference only to receiving or imprinting, but must refer also to interpretive activity in virtue of which the scene appears a certain way to him.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Setting Before the Eyes
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The concept of 'what is seen by someone as F' forms the basis for Aristotle's discussions of awareness that leads to action.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Phantasia to someone is what is seen by them as F, connecting to how things appear to sentient beings.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Being
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: In explanation of action, the philosopher must begin with how the world looks to the particular creature, not with unprocessed sensory material.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Just as in science generally the philosopher must begin with and return to the phainomena (not 'pure' or 'raw' data), so in action explanation he must begin with the way the world looks to the creature.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Recollection
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The theory of memory uses kinēseis (motions) that persist after perception and act like signet-ring impressions of aisthēmata.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle likens these kinēseis to cloud forms that resemble different things and describes them as residual traces of actual aisthēsis that make impressions.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on παράδειγμα
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle problematically suggests that phantasia activity is quasi-visual and involves picture-like objects that symbolize through similarity.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The triangle example uses the phrase 'he places before his eyes' and presents picturing and similarity as central cases.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Rhetorical Being
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: In many cases of imagining, there is never more content than what the imaginer intentionally put in.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Sartre, Ishiguro, and possibly Wittgenstein claim imagining is like sketching without stepping back to see what one has made; an image has just the content with which we invest it.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on φαντασία
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Phantasia is the faculty in virtue of which the animal sees his object as an object of a certain sort, giving perception potentially motivating content.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The use of phantasia in action-contexts and its broad connection with phainetai throughout Aristotle suggest this interpretation.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Emotion
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Phantasia works by presenting the animal with the form or essence of its object, which has an effect like that of the object itself.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle states this at MA 701b19ff and 703b19ff, calling the forms presented 'of the pleasant or painful' or 'of that which produces the affections'.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Locomotion
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Motion always requires both phantasia and desire together.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: DA 432b15 states motion occurs with both phantasia and orexis; 433b26-30 says animals cannot desire without phantasia.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Movement / Change
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Motion always requires both phantasia and desire together.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: DA 432b15 states motion occurs with both phantasia and orexis; 433b26-30 says animals cannot desire without phantasia.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Motion / Change
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Lower 'incomplete creatures' must possess both epithumia and some vague phantasia to explain their motion, not just aisthesis and epithumia alone.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: DA III.11 discusses incomplete animals, concluding they must have phantasia since they move, though Aristotle grants this grudgingly.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on βουλευτικόν
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The deliberative phantasia (bouleutike) is the species peculiar to rational creatures, distinct from the general type.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: DA III.11 distinguishes bouleutike phantasia and provides an example of its functioning.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on δύναμις
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Three inferences follow from aisthetikon and phantastikon being the 'same' capacity: (1) all perceivers can have phantasia with same physiological apparatus; (2) many aisthesis activities can be viewed as phantasia activities; (3) using both terms provides new information about the disposition.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: These follow from Aristotle's statement about sameness and difference in einai.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on δύναμις / ἐνέργεια
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The 'sameness but different einai' relationship likely means activities can be described as exercises of either capacity depending on the aspect to which we attend, not merely that they share a base capacity.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle uses phantastikon and aisthetikon (capacities) rather than phantasia and aisthesis (activities); parallel passages use difference in einai for two-description cases like the road up/down.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on τὰ ἴδια αἰσθητά
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aisthesis is affected by things that have color, taste, or sound not insofar as they are what each is spoken of as being, but insofar as they possess a certain quality.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle states this at DA 424b21ff to explain what aisthesis receives.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on αἴσθησις
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aisthesis is affected by things that have color, taste, or sound not insofar as they are what each is spoken of as being, but insofar as they possess a certain quality.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle states this at DA 424b21ff to explain what aisthesis receives.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on φαντασία βουλευτική / αἰσθητική
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle's interest in phantasia concerns how an object or state of affairs registers with a creature and what content it has for them
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The range of passages shows concern with how things are interpreted by living creatures rather than with mental imagery

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on κοινὰ αἰσθητά
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Phantasma in Plato can describe both sensory and non-sensory appearing
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: In Symposium 211a5ff., phantazesthai describes how the Form of Beauty appears, explicitly contrasted with how perceptible objects, arguments, or knowledge appear

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Principle
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: In the MA (later than Mem.), Aristotle presents a theory of memory without images, describing it as awareness of things themselves as eidōla (shadows/no longer extant).
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The MA refers to memory as awareness of pleasant and painful things in the world as shadows, suggesting a non-pictorial account.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Memory
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The theory of memory uses kinēseis (motions) that persist after perception and act like signet-ring impressions of aisthēmata.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle likens these kinēseis to cloud forms that resemble different things and describes them as residual traces of actual aisthēsis that make impressions.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Form
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: In DA II.12, aisthesis receives perceptible forms without matter, like wax receiving the impress of a signet-ring without the metal.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle compares aisthesis to wax at DA 424a18-19, contrasting with plants that absorb matter.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Phenomenology
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The best interpretive approach is to allow Aristotelian phantasia broad scope rather than forcing all passages to fit the most technical one.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle directs attention to a wide variety of phenomena under phantasia without always clearly distinguishing them, and the decaying-sense analysis doesn't fit the entire discussion.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on τέχνη
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Freudenthal correctly identified the transferred sense of phantasia as 'mere show,' though he missed the Rhetoric passage that strengthens this interpretation.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Freudenthal observed that phantasia meant 'pomp, ostentatiousness' by Aristotle's time, and the Rhetoric passage confirms Aristotle's awareness of this usage.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on ὄρεξις
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aisthesis by itself is insufficient to present the object in a way that moves the animal to act; instead it must 'prepare' a phantasia which in turn 'prepares' the desire.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: This must be explained against the background of Aristotle's theory of aisthesis to make the hypothesis convincing.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on ἀλλοίωσις
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Phantasia is accompanied of necessity by some bodily change, but the nature of the alteration is much less evident than with aisthesis.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle infers from the fact that phantasia alone, in the object's absence, can result in motion that it must involve bodily change.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on εἶδος
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: In DA II.12, aisthesis receives perceptible forms without matter, like wax receiving the impress of a signet-ring without the metal.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle compares aisthesis to wax at DA 424a18-19, contrasting with plants that absorb matter.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on ψόφος
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: In DA II.8, voice differs from mere noise because the striker must be a living creature with phantasia; voice is noise that is indicative (semantikos) of something.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle distinguishes voice from noise at DA 420b31ff by requiring phantasia.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Logos
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: In DA II.8, voice differs from mere noise because the striker must be a living creature with phantasia; voice is noise that is indicative (semantikos) of something.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle distinguishes voice from noise at DA 420b31ff by requiring phantasia.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Common Sense
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Reception and interpretation are not separable but thoroughly interdependent in perception.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aisthesis and phantasia being 'the same faculty' implies there is no receptive 'innocent eye' in perception, and how something appears to me is bound up with my past, prejudices, and needs.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on End / Final Cause
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle could solve the over-complexity problem by adopting for thinking the functional account he gives for other life-processes, but good reasons prevent this.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: There are good non-arbitrary reasons connected with his theory of action and responsibility that prevent adopting the view that thinking is a functional state of matter.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on φρόνησις
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Deliberative phantasia involves measuring using a single criterion and making one phantasma out of many.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The agent must determine whether to do this or that through reasoning, seeking the greater good.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Practical Wisdom
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Deliberative phantasia involves measuring using a single criterion and making one phantasma out of many.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The agent must determine whether to do this or that through reasoning, seeking the greater good.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Character
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Deliberative phantasia involves measuring using a single criterion and making one phantasma out of many.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The agent must determine whether to do this or that through reasoning, seeking the greater good.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on γνώμη
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Deliberative phantasia involves measuring using a single criterion and making one phantasma out of many.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The agent must determine whether to do this or that through reasoning, seeking the greater good.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Thought / Intellect
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Thinking by itself is insufficient to lead to action; the object of thought must be present to awareness as an object of desire.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle insists on this in both DA III.9 and MA 6-7.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on End/Purpose
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Thinking by itself is insufficient to lead to action; the object of thought must be present to awareness as an object of desire.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle insists on this in both DA III.9 and MA 6-7.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Intellect
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: All thinking, theoretical as well as practical, is necessarily accompanied by some activity of phantasia.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: There is no thinking that is simply abstract; every thought has some episode of symbolizing or envisaging that provides a concrete vehicle for the thought.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Hypothetical Necessity
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle's denial that thinking is physical commits him to a messy over-complexity requiring an extra phantasia in practical cases.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The thought of the sun's true size must be accompanied by symbolizing that is likely the same as the pre-judgmental phantasia seeing it as a foot wide, yet action theory forces insertion of an extra phantasia.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Nussbaum on Subjekt (subject)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Interpretive activity in perception depends on the creature's natural endowment, past, and other present activities.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle saw that this activity is dependent not only on natural endowment but also on past and other present activities.

tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Rhetorical energeia presupposes metaphysical sense (activity/aliveness as mode of being)
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Metaphysical sense is abstract and atemporal (priority thesis); rhetorical sense is concrete and perceptual (vividness)
tensionEdges.description: Whether the Rhetoric's energeia is a genuine application of the Metaphysics concept or a homonymous appropriation. The transfer from ontological priority to aesthetic vividness is Aristotle's most striking conceptual redeployment, and the mechanism of connection is never made explicit.

tensionEdges.nodeA: psyche (DA II.1: first entelecheia of natural body; inseparable from body)
tensionEdges.nodeB: nous (DA III.5: active nous is separable, immortal, eternal)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Nous is a capacity of soul; hylomorphic definition should govern all psychic capacities
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Active nous breaches the hylomorphic framework: separable, immortal, eternal (430a17-22)
tensionEdges.description: The fundamental tension of De Anima. The hylomorphic definition that governs all other psychic faculties is violated at the highest point. Reverberates into Met Lambda (divine self-thinking) and the theological tradition.

tensionEdges.nodeA: kinesis (Phys III.2: energeia ateles, incomplete actuality)
tensionEdges.nodeB: energeia (Met Theta.8: actuality prior in formula, time, substance)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Physics definition deploys the actuality concept from Metaphysics Theta
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Incomplete actuality is paradoxical within a framework where actuality = completion
tensionEdges.description: The central interpretive crux connecting Physics and Metaphysics. Whether kinesis constitutes a genuine third ontological category between potentiality and completed actuality, or is merely a conceptual device, remains the most debated question in Aristotle's process ontology.

tensionEdges.nodeA: phantasia (DA III.3: kinesis from actual sensation — causally derived)
tensionEdges.nodeB: phantasia (DA/Rhet/Mem/MA: functionally autonomous in dreams, deliberation, rhetoric, involuntary movement)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Phantasia originates in sensation and inherits its reliability structure
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: A causally dependent capacity achieves operational independence across all four application domains
tensionEdges.description: Phantasia's causal derivation from sensation conflicts with its functional autonomy in four domains: dreaming (DA), rhetorical reception (Rhet pro ommaton poiein), memory retention (Mem phantasma as likeness), and involuntary physiology (MA blushing/trembling). How a dependent capacity achieves independence is raised but never resolved.

tensionEdges.nodeA: telos (Phys II.8: nature acts for an end without deliberating)
tensionEdges.nodeB: techne (Phys II.8: art acts purposively through deliberation)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Teleological argument relies on art-nature analogy
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Stripping deliberation while retaining purposiveness undermines the analogy
tensionEdges.description: Whether non-deliberative purposiveness is genuinely explanatory or covertly metaphorical. Extends to Movement of Animals where the practical syllogism compresses deliberative structure to vanishing point in rapid action.

tensionEdges.nodeA: practical syllogism (MA ch. 7: universal major + particular minor = action)
tensionEdges.nodeB: orexis (MA/DA: desire as proximate efficient cause of locomotion)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: The practical syllogism formalizes the desire-perception-action chain
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: The conclusion is an action, not a proposition; rapid-action cases compress deliberation to nothing
tensionEdges.description: Whether the practical syllogism is a genuine logical form or a psychological causal sequence dressed in logical language. Bridges logic and psychology in a way that threatens the integrity of both.

tensionEdges.nodeA: nous (DA III.4: impassible, unmixed, without nature of its own)
tensionEdges.nodeB: phantasma (DA III.7: the soul never thinks without an image)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Nous depends on phantasmata for all operations
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Phantasmata are bodily residues of sensation; nous is supposed to be free of bodily determination
tensionEdges.description: The wax-signet model applied to both sense and thought threatens to collapse the distinction between embodied perception and separable intellection. If nous genuinely requires bodily images, its separability claim is undermined.

tensionEdges.nodeB: to_agathon (Met Lambda.10: the good as both separate principle and immanent cosmic order)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: God's thinking is the supreme actuality; the universe's order depends on it
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: A self-thinking god has no cognition of the world he orders
tensionEdges.description: How a self-thinking god can govern worldly order without cognizing it. If God thinks only himself, the mechanism by which divine thought structures cosmic order is opaque.

tensionEdges.nodeA: eidos (Met Z.viii: man generates man — form shared across instances)
tensionEdges.nodeB: eidos (Met Z.xiii: no universal is substance — form must be individual)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Form is substance; substance must be a 'this' not a 'such'
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: If form is numerically the same across instances it is universal; if numerically distinct, what individuates it?
tensionEdges.description: The fundamental tension of Metaphysics Z, never resolved. The Categories' treatment of individual composites as primary substance adds a further layer. Whether Aristotle's mature position is that individual forms are particular is one of the most debated questions in Aristotle scholarship.

tensionEdges.nodeA: chronos (Phys IV.11: number of motion — grounded in motion, mind-independent)
tensionEdges.nodeB: chronos (Phys IV.14: time qua numbered requires soul as counter)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Time is defined through motion but counting requires psyche
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Ambiguous ontological status: mind-independent or mind-dependent?
tensionEdges.description: Extends to On Memory where time is the necessary condition of memory and only time-perceiving animals can remember, binding physics to psychology. Aristotle hedges: motion can exist without soul, but time as numbered cannot.

tensionEdges.nodeA: rhetorike (Rhet I.1: morally neutral capacity that can be misused)
tensionEdges.nodeB: rhetorike (Rhet I.1: truth and justice are naturally stronger)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Rhetoric is a genuine techne with systematic rational structure
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: Value-neutrality claim conflicts with truth-orientation; art-concealing-art deepens paradox
tensionEdges.description: The constitutive tension of the Rhetoric. If truth is naturally stronger, rhetoric should be superfluous; if rhetoric is needed, truth's natural strength is insufficient. The naturalness principle (art concealing art) makes the most truthful-seeming speech the most artfully constructed.

tensionEdges.nodeA: phantasma (Mem: object of contemplation in itself, theorema)
tensionEdges.nodeB: phantasma (Mem: likeness of the thing remembered, eikon)
tensionEdges.dependencyRelation: Memory consists in perceiving the phantasma qua likeness
tensionEdges.conflictRelation: The shift from in-itself to qua-likeness presupposes awareness of the absent original it explains
tensionEdges.description: The representational puzzle at the heart of Aristotle's philosophy of mind. How does the soul recognize a present image as a likeness of an absent thing without already having access to the absent thing? This is the Aristotelian anticipation of the modern problem of intentionality.
Readiness-to-hand is ontologically prior, yet presence-at-hand is what the tradition takes as the default mode of Being. The contrast is both structural and critical.
Das Man is a necessary existentiale, yet authenticity requires wresting oneself from it. Dependence + opposition = productive tension.
Disclosedness is Dasein's 'there,' but falling is equally constitutive and works against disclosure. The 'there' both reveals and conceals.
Care is the being of Dasein (Division One), but temporality reinterprets it at a deeper level (Division Two). The 'same' structure shifts meaning.
Death individualizes absolutely, yet Dasein is essentially Being-with. The tension between radical singularity and constitutive sociality is never fully resolved.
Within-time-ness is genuinely derived from originary temporality, yet it systematically conceals its own origin. Derivation + concealment.
Dasein is simultaneously thrown (already-in) and projecting (ahead-of-itself). These are co-original moments of care that pull in opposite temporal directions.
Dasein is its possibilities (existence) yet always already determined (facticity). Neither can be reduced to the other; their unity is care.
Assertion depends on interpretation but transforms it. The logical tradition mistakes the derivative for the primordial.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.description: Movement IS the presence (ἐντελέχεια) of what is able to be there precisely insofar as it is not yet completed (ἐνέργεια). The equivocation is ontologically necessary.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.description: Meaningfulness (Bedeutsamkeit) and potentiality are two faces of the same phenomenon. The world is encountered as meaningful-available-for, and this availability constitutes the from...toward... structure of movement.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.description: Conceptuality has a 'double sense' precisely because the same λόγος that discloses also conceals. The fore-structures must be both overcome and appropriated. This tension drives the entire Second Part.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.description: Theoretical science arises from and against the background of δόξα. Science is the transformation, not the abolition, of everyday opinion.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.description: Neither is simply more fundamental. They are equiprimordial (gleichursprünglich) -- anticipating BT's analysis of Rede, Befindlichkeit, and Verstehen as co-original existentialia.

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.nodeA: ἀρετή as μεσότης (the mean πρὸς ἡμᾶς)
tensionEdges.nodeB: ἀρετή as ἀκρότης (the highest with regard to the εὖ)
tensionEdges.description: The tension dissolves when μεσότης is understood as a way of being-composed (the 'how') rather than a quantitative midpoint. The mean is the extreme because it is the mode of being most genuinely related to the concrete situation (καιρός).

tensionEdges.text: Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy
tensionEdges.description: The non-parallelism shows that dispositions are not reactions to pre-given objects but disclosive modes of being-in-the-world. The gap between φοβερά and φόβος makes fear a finding-oneself rather than a causal response.

Withdrawal is not the enemy of disclosure but its enabling condition; the world's inexhaustibility (its always-exceeding what we make of it) ensures rhetoric is never finished, always preparatory, always calling for further attunement. Withdrawal grounds rhetoric's inexhaustibility.

Rickert does not eliminate subjectivity but reconceives it as emplaced and distributed, preventing ambient rhetoric from collapsing into undifferentiated flat ontology while insisting that agency is never solely human.

Attunement redefines rather than eliminates skilled practice: the rhetor is seized by the moment rather than seizing it, but this requires a cultivated receptivity (ear cleaning, trust in the moment) that is itself a form of non-sovereign expertise.

Networks are necessary but insufficient: they correctly grasp the ontological character of relationality, but ambience adds the immersive, osmotic, choric thickness that the network metaphor cannot provide, driving the move from Part 1 to Part 2.

Rickert harvests Burke for the richness of social drama and embodied rhetoric while correcting him with Heidegger's more radical decentering; together they establish that meaning inheres in the world but disagree on whether humans remain the gravitational center of language.

Technology is both the condition under which ambient rhetoric becomes visible and the principal obstacle to genuine dwelling; ambient rhetoric requires not anti-technology but a transformed relation to technology grounded in dwelling rather than efficiency.

Rickert needs both: Latour's concrete demonstrations of material persuasion and Heidegger's deeper ontological framework. Dingpolitik does not come first through extending politics but emerges from dwelling as attunement -- the political is grounded in the ontological.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The subject is defined against mechanism, yet the Funktionskreis -- the core analytical unit -- employs mechanistic vocabulary (receptor, effector, reflex arc). Uexkuell reinterprets but never fully escapes the machine idiom.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: Uexkuell strips teleological goal-language from biology but replaces it with 'Nature's plan' -- a concept that smuggles purposiveness back in under a different name. 'Nature knows how to deal with difficulties' is itself anthropomorphic.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The Theory of Meaning oscillates between constructivism (meaning is impressed by the subject) and pre-established harmony (the Komplement-Bauplan fit implies a prior design that the subject merely activates).

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The search image is simultaneously a perception image and its antagonist. Composed of the same materials (perception signs), it can erase the very perception image it resembles, making the boundary between subject-generated and stimulus-driven perception unstable.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The magical environment contradicts the stimulus-response architecture of the Funktionskreis. Early chapters build the functional cycle on perception marks from external objects; the magical chapter shows perception images arising without any object -- a free production of the subject that the original schema cannot accommodate.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: Uexkuell's perspectivism declares Nature unknowable, yet the biologist who writes about tick and spider Umwelten implicitly occupies a meta-perspectival position. The reflexivity problem -- how the Umwelt theorist escapes his own Umwelt -- is never resolved.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The Kompositionslehre replaces causal explanation with contrapuntal description but never clarifies the ontological status of the meaning rule. It is not a force, not a substance, not a causal chain -- yet governs embryogenesis, cross-species adaptation, and ecological composition. Musical metaphor does real work but risks substituting analogy for explanation.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The concept of Bedeutungsduldung introduces radical passivity into a framework built on subject-constituted worlds. The fly in the spider's web and the plant being grazed are subjects whose Umwelt is violated by another subject's meaning-conferral. Active subject-constitution and passive meaning-sufferance coexist without reconciliation.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: Naturtechnik promises a science of compositional principles, yet its central object -- the formative melody -- is declared inscrutable. The genes are keys, the protoplasm is material, but the melody that plays upon them is invisible. This positions Uexkuell's biology between empirical science and avowed mystery.

tensionEdges.text: Von Uexkull - A Foray into the Worlds of Animals and Humans
tensionEdges.description: The anti-Darwinian stance and the Kompositionslehre share the same evidential base -- mutual organism-environment fitness -- but interpret it oppositely. Darwin sees emergent adaptation through selection; Uexkuell sees pre-composed contrapuntal harmony. The choice between them cannot be settled by the examples alone.
